Let \(A=x\), so \(C=3x\). From the Law of Sines:

\[
\frac{27}{\sin x}=\frac{48}{\sin 3x}
\implies \frac{\sin x}{\sin 3x}=\frac{9}{16}.
\]

Using \(\sin 3x=3\sin x-4\sin^3 x\),

\[
\frac{\sin x}{3\sin x-4\sin^3 x}=\frac{9}{16}
\implies \frac{1}{3-4\sin^2 x}=\frac{9}{16}.
\]

Thus

\[
16=27-36\sin^2 x \implies \sin^2 x=\frac{11}{36}.
\]

So \(\sin x=\frac{\sqrt{11}}6\) and \(\cos x=\frac56\).

Then

\[
\sin 4x=2\sin 2x\cos 2x
=2\left(2\sin x\cos x\right)\left(\cos^2 x-\sin^2 x\right)
=\frac{35\sqrt{11}}{162}.
\]

Since

\[
\frac{a}{\sin A}=\frac{27}{\sin x}=\frac{162}{\sqrt{11}},
\]

we get

\[
b=\frac{162}{\sqrt{11}}\sin B
=\frac{162}{\sqrt{11}}\sin(180^\circ-4x)
=\frac{162}{\sqrt{11}}\sin 4x
=35.
\]

\[
\boxed{35}
\]
